svg.text: Everyday English - Grammar
Would rather with another
subject
MEANING
Use would rather + subject + past form to express
a present or future preference about someone
else’s action.
IN CONTEXT
I would rather we discussed the details tomorrow.
USAGE NOTE
The past form marks a preference, not past time.
Same subject: I would rather wait. Different
subject: I would rather you waited. Negative: I
would rather you did not rush.
CONVERSATION
A: Shall I send the report now?
B: I would rather you checked the figures first.
A: You mean before sending it, not that I checked
them yesterday?
B: Exactly. The past form expresses my
preference about what you do next.
YOUR TURN
Rewrite politely: I prefer that you do not change
the schedule. Use would rather.
